name: OpenBioLLM 70B
usecase: Top-performing open medical LLM. Outperforms GPT-4 on several medical benchmarks. Best choice when accuracy is critical.
strength: USMLE, MedQA, PubMedQA — best-in-class open model across all three.

name: Meditron 70B
usecase: High-accuracy clinical reasoning at scale. Trained on medical guidelines, clinical practice papers, and PubMed.
strength: Complex multi-step clinical reasoning, medical exam benchmarks, research pipelines.

name: Med42 70B
usecase: Clinical AI designed with patient safety guardrails by healthcare professionals. Medically verified responses.
strength: Clinical vignettes, drug interactions, triage support, safety-conscious outputs.

name: MedGemma 27B
usecase: Google's latest health-focused model. Strong on medical QA and clinical reasoning with multimodal capability (text + images).
strength: Medical VQA, radiology report understanding, clinical reasoning, multimodal health tasks.

name: MedGemma 4B
usecase: Lightweight multimodal health model for edge deployment. Handles both text and medical images.
strength: On-device health apps, chest X-ray analysis, fast clinical QA with low resource footprint.

name: BioMistral 7B
usecase: Biomedical text understanding and generation. Pre-trained on PubMed Central full-text. Best open-source mid-size option.
strength: Biomedical NER, relation extraction, literature QA — strong open-source choice.

name: Meditron 7B
usecase: Medical exam prep and clinical Q&A. Fine-tuned on medical guidelines, textbooks, and clinical practice papers.
strength: USMLE-style questions, clinical decision support, drug-disease reasoning on consumer hardware.

name: OpenBioLLM 8B
usecase: High-performance medical LLM that runs on consumer hardware. Best balance of accuracy and resource use.
strength: Medical QA, clinical reasoning — strong performance without requiring a 70B setup.

name: Asclepius 7B
usecase: Trained on synthetic clinical notes generated from MIMIC-III. Specialised for clinical documentation tasks.
strength: Clinical note understanding, discharge summary generation, EHR-based QA.

name: HuatuoGPT-II 7B
usecase: Bilingual (Chinese/English) medical LLM. Strong at doctor-patient dialogue and clinical consultation.
strength: Medical consultation, symptom elicitation, patient-facing health conversations.

name: ChatDoctor 7B
usecase: Patient-facing medical chatbot fine-tuned on 100k real doctor-patient conversations from HealthCareMagic.
strength: Symptom discussion, patient education, general health Q&A in conversational format.

name: MedAlpaca 13B
usecase: Medical instruction following for QA and patient-facing applications. Trained on Alpaca-style medical dialogues.
strength: Conversational medical QA, patient education, symptom explanation.

name: PMC-LLaMA 13B
usecase: Biomedical literature understanding. Fine-tuned on 4.8M PubMed abstracts and 100k+ PubMed Central papers.
strength: Research paper QA, evidence synthesis, biomedical fact extraction from literature.

name: ClinicalCamel 30B
usecase: Clinical note generation and EHR-style text processing. Trained on USMLE and clinical dialogue datasets.
strength: Clinical documentation, discharge summaries, clinical reasoning from patient histories.

name: BioGPT
usecase: Biomedical text generation and question answering. Pre-trained on 15M PubMed abstracts.
strength: Relation extraction, biomedical NER, PubMed-grounded QA. Very lightweight and fast.

name: BioBERT Large
usecase: The workhorse of biomedical NLP. Best for named entity recognition, relation extraction, and text classification.
strength: Disease NER, drug-drug interaction detection, biomedical text classification pipelines.

name: ClinicalBERT
usecase: Clinical note understanding. Trained on MIMIC-III discharge summaries. Best for EHR-derived NLP tasks.
strength: Clinical NER, ICD coding assistance, clinical text classification from free-text notes.

name: PubMedBERT
usecase: Pre-trained from scratch on PubMed. Superior to general BERT for all biomedical downstream tasks.
strength: Biomedical NLI, NER, text classification, sentence embeddings for retrieval.

name: BioLinkBERT
usecase: BioBERT variant that leverages document links for richer biomedical knowledge. State-of-the-art on many bio NLP benchmarks.
strength: Biomedical QA, NER, semantic similarity — especially strong when citation/link context matters.

name: SapBERT
usecase: Self-alignment pre-training for biomedical entity representations. Excels at linking clinical mentions to ontology concepts.
strength: Medical entity linking, UMLS concept normalisation, clinical NER post-processing.

name: GatorTron 3.9B
usecase: Large clinical model trained on 90B words of de-identified EHR text from UF Health.
strength: Clinical concept extraction, medical NLI, clinical text classification from real EHR data.

name: BlueBERT
usecase: Joint biomedical and clinical NLP. Trained on both PubMed and MIMIC-III for cross-domain tasks.
strength: NER tasks bridging research literature and clinical notes. Good for cross-domain health NLP.

name: Clinical Longformer
usecase: Processes long clinical documents (up to 4096 tokens). Best for discharge summaries, operative notes, full patient records.
strength: Long clinical note classification, full-document EHR analysis, ICD coding from complete notes.

name: SciBERT
usecase: Scientific text understanding across all domains. Good baseline for health research NLP without domain-specific pre-training.
strength: Scientific NER, citation classification, research paper classification.

name: LLaVA-Med
usecase: Multimodal medical model for image + text understanding. Trained on biomedical figure-caption pairs from PubMed.
strength: Medical VQA, biomedical image captioning, radiology report QA.

name: LLaMA 3.1 8B
usecase: Strong general-purpose base for health RAG pipelines. Excellent instruction following for structured clinical output.
strength: Health RAG, structured JSON output, clinical report summarization.

name: Mistral 7B
usecase: Efficient general model widely used as base for medical fine-tuning. Great for health RAG with structured retrieval.
strength: Fast inference, solid reasoning, good JSON compliance for structured health data output.

name: Gemma 2 9B
usecase: High-quality reasoning in a mid-size model. Performs well above its weight class on medical QA benchmarks.
strength: Clinical reasoning, health claim verification, evidence appraisal.

name: Qwen 2.5 7B
usecase: Excellent structured output reliability. Great for health RAG pipelines requiring consistent JSON responses.
strength: JSON reliability, multilingual health content, structured data extraction.

name: Phi-3.5 Mini
usecase: Best small model for health use cases. Runs on edge devices and mobile. Strong medical reasoning for its size.
strength: On-device health apps, offline triage tools, low-latency clinical chatbots.

name: Zephyr 7B Beta
usecase: Strong instruct-tuned general model often used as base for health fine-tuning. Reliable, well-aligned responses.
strength: Health RAG baseline, medical content generation, easy to fine-tune for specific clinical tasks.

name: Qwen 2.5 72B
usecase: High-capability general model competitive with GPT-4 on many tasks. Excellent for health research and complex clinical reasoning.
strength: Complex clinical reasoning, research synthesis, multilingual health content at scale.

name: Bio-Medical LLaMA 3 8B
usecase: Llama 3 fine-tuned on a curated biomedical corpus covering clinical guidelines, PubMed, and medical Q&A pairs.
strength: Biomedical question answering, clinical text generation, medical knowledge retrieval tasks.

name: Medical Qwen3 Swallow 8B
usecase: Japanese and English medical LLM fine-tuned from Qwen3. Strong on medical licensing exam questions and clinical reasoning in both languages.
strength: Bilingual (JA/EN) medical QA, Japanese clinical guidelines, medical exam preparation.

name: Mental Health Counseling Falcon 7B
usecase: Falcon 7B fine-tuned on mental health counseling conversations. Designed for empathetic, supportive dialogue.
strength: Mental health support conversations, crisis response drafting, therapeutic dialogue simulation.

name: Mental Health Chatbot LLaMA 2 13B
usecase: LLaMA 2 13B fine-tuned specifically for mental health conversation. Larger capacity for nuanced empathetic responses.
strength: Mental health counseling, anxiety/depression support conversations, empathetic text generation.

name: Healix 3B
usecase: Lightweight health-focused model optimised for patient-facing applications and healthcare Q&A with low latency.
strength: Fast health Q&A, patient education, symptom description — ideal for low-resource deployments.

name: UMLSBert
usecase: BERT pre-trained with UMLS knowledge graph supervision. Excels at medical concept normalisation and clinical NLP.
strength: UMLS concept linking, clinical abbreviation disambiguation, medical entity normalisation.

name: CheXbert
usecase: BERT fine-tuned on radiology reports for automated chest X-ray label extraction. Used in radiology NLP pipelines.
strength: Automated radiology report labelling, CheXpert label prediction, chest X-ray findings extraction.

name: MedCPT Query Encoder
usecase: Zero-shot biomedical retrieval model trained by NCBI. Encodes medical queries and articles for semantic search.
strength: Medical RAG pipelines, PubMed article retrieval, biomedical semantic search — purpose-built for health retrieval.

name: BioELECTRA Large
usecase: ELECTRA architecture pre-trained on PubMed. More sample-efficient than BioBERT for most biomedical NLP tasks.
strength: Biomedical NER, text classification — trains faster and often outperforms BioBERT on small datasets.

name: CXR-BERT
usecase: BERT pre-trained on radiology reports from MIMIC-CXR. Specialized for chest X-ray report understanding and generation.
strength: Radiology report NLP, chest X-ray findings classification, visual-language alignment for radiology.

name: Clinical T5 Large
usecase: T5 pre-trained on MIMIC-III clinical notes. Generative model for clinical text tasks including summarization and Q&A.
strength: Clinical note summarization, discharge summary generation, clinical text-to-text tasks.

name: Llama 3 Aloe 8B
usecase: Medical LLM with safety alignment from Barcelona Supercomputing Center. Trained on curated medical corpus with safety guardrails.
strength: Safe clinical reasoning, medical QA with refusal handling, European clinical guidelines.

name: BioMistral MedNER 7B
usecase: DARE-merged variant of BioMistral with improved instruction following. Better for structured extraction tasks.
strength: Biomedical NER, structured medical output, drug/disease/gene extraction.
